standard.title: Interpret information displayed in different formats
standard.description: interpret information and data displayed in different formats
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2S03): Students interpreted distance and location on maps and compared objects and activities across places and time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information and data displayed in different formats including climate data, maps, graphs and photographs.

nodes.label: Distinguishing fiction from non-fiction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between fiction and non-fiction texts in relation to their representation of places, environments and past events.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify whether a given text about a place or past event is fiction or non-fiction and explain one reason for the distinction.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish fiction from non-fiction in texts about places, environments and past events; discuss how each type of text can be useful in HASS inquiry for different purposes.
wider: Identify how a historical fiction text uses factual details and which elements are invented
Explore how point of view affects whether a source presents events as fact or interpretation
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot distinguish fiction from non-fiction cannot correctly assess the evidentiary value of sources — this is a prerequisite for all subsequent analysis.

response_modes.reason: The fiction/non-fiction distinction requires criteria — explicitly teach the features that distinguish each type in HASS contexts.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies a given text as fiction or non-fiction
Gives at least one reason for the classification

nodes.label: Interpreting climate data, graphs and maps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret climate data, graphs, maps and photographs to identify patterns and features.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least one data display (graph, table, map or photograph) to identify one pattern or feature.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret climate data to describe temperature and rainfall for a place; interpret data to identify patterns of change over time; use maps, aerial photographs and satellite images to identify and describe features including cartographic elements.
wider: Compare climate data from two contrasting places and draw conclusions about how climate affects human activity
Interpret building date data to make inferences about changing architectural styles and materials

response_modes.reason: Interpreting across multiple data formats (graphs, maps, photographs, tables) builds transferable analytical skill.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Each data format requires different interpretation strategies — building fluency across formats creates genuinely more capable data analysts.
success_criteria: Interprets at least one data display accurately
Identifies at least one pattern or feature from the display
